tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). """Session memory: any model gets "how you solved similar things before".

No training. Every past task (one real user prompt + what followed: files
edited, commands run, how it ended) from Claude Code and OpenCode goes into a
local index (~/.footprint/memory.json, rebuilt incrementally). On each new
prompt, `footprint recall` finds the closest past tasks (BM25, stdlib) and
prints a short brief that the Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook / OpenCode
plugin adds to the conversation.

  footprint recall "add a year limit to the date picker"   # try it by hand
"""
import glob, hashlib, json, math, os, re, sqlite3, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime

from . import bench, config, context, transcripts

INDEX = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/memory.json")
EMBEDS = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/embed.json")
FORGOTTEN = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/forgotten.json")  # fact ids the user removed (footprint memory forget)
ARCHIVE = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/archive")  # redacted copies: outlive Claude Code's transcript cleanup
ARCHIVE_IDLE = 1800   # seconds a transcript must sit unchanged before it's copied (don't rewrite the live one per prompt)
SHOWN = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/recall")  # per-session: task ids already injected
VERSION = 3           # 2: tasks carry "corrected"; 3: bench replay prompts dropped
TOP_K = 3
MIN_SCORE = 4.0       # ponytail: fixed BM25 cutoff; tune on real prompts or switch to embeddings if recall is weak
MIN_TERMS = 2         # need at least this many shared meaningful words
STOP = set("""a an and are as at be but by can do does for from get got has have how i if in into is it its
just let lets like make me my need no not now of on or our please so some that the then there this to
up us use using want was we what when where which why will with would you your yes ok okay also all any
should could thing things right file files code add fix
show list best possible suggest based help user users their them they one some any okay cool great tell
explain give know think way work working still really something new make made did done see look""".split())
[redacted]
                    r"|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|xox[abpr]-[\w-]{10,}|eyJ[\w-]{20,}\.[\w-]{10,}\.[\w-]{10,}"
                    r"|(?i:(?:api[_-]?key|token|secret|password|passwd)\s*[=:]\s*)\S+"
                    # env-style: [redacted] [redacted] [redacted]
                    r"|\b[A-Z0-9_]*(?:SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|API_?KEY|PRIVATE_KEY|CLIENT_ID|_KEY|DATABASE_URL|DSN)"
                    r"[A-Z0-9_]*\s*=\s*\S+"
                    r"|\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://[^/\s:@]+:[^@\s]+@)")  # user:password@ in any URL


def _redact(t):
    return SECRET.sub("[redacted]", t or "")


# Pattern recognition shared by training (collect) and memory (facts / recall).
# ponytail: regex heuristics; an LLM classifier only if bench shows these labels are too noisy
CORRECTION = re.compile(r"^\W*(no\b|nope\b|wrong\b|undo\b|revert\b|stop\b|don'?t\b|do not\b|that'?s not\b|not what\b"
                        r"|why (did|are|is|would|didn'?t|didnt) (you|we|it|this)\b|why didn'?t\b|why didnt\b"
                        r"|you (broke|didn'?t|missed|forgot)\b|still\b|it'?s (not|broken|failing)\b"
                        r"|(it |this )?(doesn'?t|didn'?t|isn'?t) work"
                        r"|not working\b|this is wrong\b)|\[Request interrupted", re.I)
# standing-rule wording only; "instead of X" is almost always a one-off task instruction, not a habit
PREF = re.compile(r"\b(always|never|from now on|i prefer|prefer to|don'?t use|dont use|do not use|stop using)\b(?!-)", re.I)
FACT_MIN = 2          # a preference must recur across tasks before it is injected: once = a task, twice = a pattern
NEG = re.compile(r"\b(never|don'?t use|dont use|do not use|stop using)\b", re.I)
PREF_WORDS = set("always never prefer from don dont do not stop use using i to on".split())
RIVALS = [{"npm", "pnpm", "yarn", "bun"}, {"pip", "uv", "poetry", "pipenv", "conda"}, {"jest", "vitest", "mocha"},
          {"prettier", "biome"}, {"black", "ruff"}, {"eslint", "biome", "oxlint"}, {"postgres", "postgresql", "mysql", "sqlite", "neon", "supabase", "mongodb", "mongo"},
    out.append(HANDOFF_END)
    return "\n\n".join(out)[:config.CONTEXT_CAP]


def show(args=()):
    """`footprint context` — print previous-session state. As a hook (Claude
    SessionStart or the OpenCode plugin), reads {cwd, session_id, transcript_path?}
    JSON from stdin; by hand, uses the current directory."""
    if args and args[0] == "install":
        return install()
    hook = {}
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        try:
            hook = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass
    tp = hook.get("transcript_path")
    cwd = hook.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
    found = previous(cwd, hook.get("session_id"), os.path.dirname(tp) if tp else None)
    from . import memory
    mem = ""
    if os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MEMORY") != "off":
        tasks = memory.build(skip_sid=hook.get("session_id"))
        # standing preferences first (apply to any task), then habits + project memory. All before the
        # handover: /continue strips everything up to HANDOFF_END, so none of it is indexed as a prompt
        mem = "\n\n".join(b for b in (memory.render_facts(memory.facts(tasks, cwd)), memory.profile(tasks, cwd)) if b)
    if mem:
        print(mem + ("\n" if found else ""))
    if found:
        print(render(*found))
    elif not hook and not mem:
        print(f"no previous session within {config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H}h for {cwd}")


def install():
    """Claude Code SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit hooks, OpenCode plugin (auto), /continue command (manual)."""
    path = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/settings.json")
    try:
        cfg = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8")) if os.path.exists(path) else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        sys.exit(f"{path} is not valid JSON — fix it first, not overwriting")
    cmd = f'"{sys.executable}" "{config.ENTRY}" context'
    for event, sub, entry in (("SessionStart", "context", {"matcher": "startup|clear"}),
                              ("UserPromptSubmit", "recall", {})):  # recall = session memory per prompt
        hooks = cfg.setdefault("hooks", {}).setdefault(event, [])
        hooks[:] = [e for e in hooks if not any(f'footprint.py" {sub}' in h.get("command", "")
                                                for h in e.get("hooks", []))]
        hooks.append({**entry, "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": f'"{sys.executable}" "{config.ENTRY}" {sub}'}]})
    cfg.setdefault("cleanupPeriodDays", 3650)  # Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days by default; never override a user's choice
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
    plugin = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "plugins", "footprint.js")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(plugin), exist_ok=True)
    src = open(PLUGIN_SRC, encoding="utf-8").read()
    with open(plugin, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(src.replace("__PY__", json.dumps(sys.executable)).replace("__ENTRY__", json.dumps(config.ENTRY)))
    oc = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "commands", "continue.md")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(oc), exist_ok=True)
    with open(oc, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("---\ndescription: continue from your last session in this project, Claude Code or OpenCode (footprint)\n---\n"
                f"!`{cmd}`\n\n$ARGUMENTS\n")
    from . import memory
    tasks = memory.build()  # first index now, so the first prompt isn't slow
    n, emb = len(tasks), len(memory.embed_index(tasks, limit=len(tasks)))
    print(f"continuity on — new sessions start where the last one (Claude Code or OpenCode) left off.\n"
          f"memory on — each prompt gets similar past work from {n} indexed tasks.\n"
          + (f"semantic recall on ({config.EMBED_MODEL}).\n" if emb else
             f"semantic recall off — for it: ollama pull {config.EMBED_MODEL} && footprint recall --embed\n")
          + "archive on — redacted copies of every session in ~/.footprint/archive (Claude Code keeps transcripts 10y unless you set otherwise).\n"
          + "profile on — new sessions get preferences you repeated (footprint facts) + habits and this project's memory (footprint profile).\n"
          f"  claude code: SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit hooks in {path}\n"
          f"  opencode:    auto via plugin {plugin}\n"
          f"               /continue [task] for sessions already open ({oc})\n"
          f"  preview:     footprint context · footprint recall <text>")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check on a synthetic Claude transcript + OpenCode db
    import tempfile
    recs = [
        {"type": "ai-title", "aiTitle": "Fix login"},
        {"type": "user", "gitBranch": "main", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "fix the login bug"}},
        {"type": "assistant", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_use", "name": "Edit", "input": {"file_path": "/a.py"}},
            {"type": "tool_use", "name": "TodoWrite", "input": {"todos": [
                {"content": "add test", "status": "pending"}, {"content": "fix", "status": "completed"}]}}]}},
        {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "is_error": True, "content": "boom"}]}},
        {"type": "user", "isMeta": True, "message": {"role": "user", "content": "meta noise"}},
        {"type": "assistant", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "fixed, test next"}]}},
    ]
def profile(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Session-start block: who you are as a developer + what this project is. '' when nothing learned."""
    here = [t for t in tasks if cwd and t["cwd"] and os.path.abspath(t["cwd"]) == os.path.abspath(cwd)]
    out = []  # standing preferences come from facts() (evidence-based), not from here
    tools = Counter(h for t in tasks for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(8)
    exts = Counter(os.path.splitext(f)[1] for t in tasks for f in t["files"] if os.path.splitext(f)[1]).most_common(6)
    habits = []
    if tools:
        habits.append("tools you run: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in tools))
    if exts:
        habits.append("you mostly edit: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in exts))
    if habits:
        out.append("Habits: " + "; ".join(habits))
    from_repo = repo(cwd) if cwd and os.path.isdir(cwd) else []
    if here or from_repo:
        proj = [f"## This project: {os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(cwd))} ({len(here)} past tasks)", *from_repo]
        root = os.path.abspath(cwd) + os.sep
        hot = Counter(f[len(root):] if f.startswith(root) else f for t in here for f in t["files"]).most_common(8)
        if hot:
            proj.append("Most-edited files: " + ", ".join(f for f, _ in hot))
        tools = Counter(h for t in here for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(6)
        if tools:
            proj.append("Tools run here: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in tools))
        now = time.time()
        recent = sorted(here, key=lambda t: -t["t"])[:5]
        if recent:
            proj.append("Recent work here:\n" + "\n".join(
                f"- {(now - t['t']) / 86400:.0f}d ago: {' '.join(t['prompt'].split())[:140]}" for t in recent))
        out.append("\n".join(proj))
    if not out:
        return ""
    head = "# Your profile (footprint — learned from your past sessions; follow unless the user says otherwise)"
    return "\n\n".join([head, *out])[:config.PROFILE_CAP]


def facts(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Structured memory (schema v1): standing preferences the user stated in their own prompts.
    Derived from the task index on demand, so nothing is stored twice or goes stale.
    Same word-set across sessions = one record with more evidence; newest wording wins;
    seen in 2+ projects = user scope, else project scope. cwd filters to user + that project."""
    recs = {}
    for t in tasks:
        if kind(t["prompt"]) == "paste" or TEMP_PATH.match(t["cwd"] or "") or "/scratchpad" in (t["cwd"] or ""):
            continue  # a pasted doc's rules aren't the user's; nor are test prompts run in temp folders
        for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", t["prompt"]):
            s = s.strip(" -*>\t")
            if not (12 <= len(s) <= 200 and len(s.split()) >= 4 and PREF.search(s)) or s.startswith(("<", "{", '"')) \
                    or s.endswith("?") or '":' in s or re.search(r"never ?mind", s, re.I):
                continue
            key = " ".join(sorted(set(_words(s))))
            if not key:
                continue
            r = recs.setdefault(key, {"kind": "correction" if is_correction(t["prompt"]) else "preference",
                                      "text": s, "projects": set(), "evidence": [],
                                      "first": t["t"], "last": t["t"]})
            r["projects"].add(t["cwd"] or "?")
            r["evidence"].append(t["id"])
            r["first"] = min(r["first"], t["t"])
            if t["t"] >= r["last"]:
                r["text"], r["last"] = s, t["t"]
    here = os.path.abspath(cwd) if cwd else None
    gone = forgotten()
    day = lambda ts: datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).date().isoformat()
    now = max((t["t"] for t in tasks), default=0)  # decay against your latest activity, not the wall clock
    out = []
    for key, r in recs.items():
        n, projs = len(r["evidence"]), sorted(r["projects"])
        scope = "user" if len(projs) > 1 else f"project:{projs[0]}"
        fid = "f_" + hashlib.sha1(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
        if fid in gone:
            continue
        recency = 0.5 ** (max(0, now - r["last"]) / 86400 / HALF_LIFE)
        out.append({"id": fid, "score": round(SOURCE_W[r["kind"]] * min(1, n / 3) * recency, 3),
                    "polarity": "-" if NEG.search(r["text"]) else "+", "superseded_by": None,
                    "_fresh": recency >= STALE, "_cw": set(_words(r["text"])) - PREF_WORDS, "schema": 1, "kind": r["kind"],
                    "scope": scope, "text": r["text"], "count": n,
                    "confidence": round(min(0.95, 0.5 + 0.15 * (n - 1)), 2),  # ponytail: evidence-count prior
                    "evidence": r["evidence"][-5:], "first_seen": day(r["first"]), "last_seen": day(r["last"]),
                    "_last": r["last"]})
    # same subject, opposite polarity ("always use X" vs "never use X"): the newer one wins
    # ponytail: polarity only; "use pnpm" vs "use npm" (same polarity, rival tools) isn't caught
    # or same polarity, rival tools ("always use pnpm" then "always use bun"): the newer choice wins
    picks = lambda r, g: {w for w in g if re.search(rf"\b{w}\b", r["text"], re.I)}
    for a in out:
        for b in out:
            if a is b or a["scope"] != b["scope"] or b["_last"] <= a["_last"] or not a["_cw"]:
                continue
            flip = a["polarity"] != b["polarity"] and len(a["_cw"] & b["_cw"]) / len(a["_cw"] | b["_cw"]) >= 0.5
            rival = a["polarity"] == b["polarity"] == "+" and any(
                (pa := picks(a, g)) and (pb := picks(b, g)) and not pa & pb for g in RIVALS)
            if flip or rival:
                a["superseded_by"] = b["id"]
    for r in out:
        r["active"] = r["count"] >= FACT_MIN and not r["superseded_by"] and r.pop("_fresh")
        del r["_cw"]
    out = [r for r in out if not here or r["scope"] in ("user", f"project:{here}")]
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["active"], r["score"], r.pop("_last")), reverse=True)
    return out


def render_facts(recs, cap=1200):
    recs = [r for r in recs if r["active"]][:12]
    if not recs:
        return ""
    lines = ["# Standing preferences (footprint memory — stated by this user in past sessions; "
             "follow unless told otherwise)"]
    lines += [f"- {r['text']}" + (f" (x{r['count']})" if r["count"] > 1 else "") for r in recs]
    return "\n".join(lines)[:cap]


def facts_cmd(args=()):
    """`footprint facts [--all]` — structured memory as JSON (this project + user-wide; --all = every project)."""
    print(json.dumps(facts(build(), None if "--all" in args else os.getcwd()), indent=2))


def forgotten():
    try:
        return set(json.load(open(FORGOTTEN, encoding="utf-8")))


def memory_cmd(args=()):
    """`footprint memory list [--all]` — what new sessions are told about you; `forget <id>...` removes a wrong one."""
    sub, rest = (args[0] if args else "list"), list(args[1:])
    if sub == "forget":
        known = {f["id"] for f in facts(build())}
        ids = [i for i in rest if i in known]
        for i in set(rest) - known:
            print(f"unknown id {i} (see: footprint memory list --all)")
        if ids:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(FORGOTTEN), exist_ok=True)
            json.dump(sorted(forgotten() | set(ids)), open(FORGOTTEN, "w", encoding="utf-8"))
            print(f"forgot {len(ids)}: never injected again")
        return
    if sub == "eval":
        return print(evaluate(build(), os.getcwd()))
    if sub == "review":
        return review(build(), rest)
    if sub != "list":
        sys.exit("usage: footprint memory list [--all] | forget <id>... | review | eval")
    tasks, cwd = build(), os.getcwd()
    fs = facts(tasks, None if "--all" in rest else cwd)
    print("Standing preferences (injected at session start when seen x%d+):" % FACT_MIN)
    for f in fs:
        why = "on " if f["active"] else "replaced" if f["superseded_by"] else "once" if f["count"] < FACT_MIN else "stale"
        print(f"  [{why:<8}] {f['id']}  x{f['count']}  score {f['score']:.2f}  "
              f"{f['scope'].replace('project:', '')[-30:]:<30}  {f['text'][:90]}")
    if not fs:
        print("  (none yet)")
    print()
    print(profile(tasks, cwd) or "No profile yet.")
    if forgotten():
        print(f"\n{len(forgotten())} forgotten (edit {FORGOTTEN} to undo)")


def recall(args=()):
    """`footprint recall` — hook mode reads {prompt, cwd, session_id} JSON on stdin
    (Claude UserPromptSubmit / OpenCode plugin); by hand: footprint recall <text>."""
    hook = {}
    if args == ["--embed"]:
        tasks = build()
        n = len(embed_index(tasks, limit=len(tasks)))
        return print(f"{n}/{len({t['id'] for t in tasks})} tasks embedded with {config.EMBED_MODEL}" if n else
                     f"no embeddings — is Ollama running? try: ollama pull {config.EMBED_MODEL}")
    if args:
        hook = {"prompt": " ".join(args), "cwd": os.getcwd()}
    elif not sys.stdin.isatty():
        try:
            hook = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return
    prompt, sid = hook.get("prompt") or "", hook.get("session_id")
    if (os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MEMORY") == "off" or not prompt.strip() or context.HANDOFF_END in prompt
            or prompt.lstrip().startswith(context.NOISE)):  # harness messages (task notifications) aren't asks
        return
    shown_f = os.path.join(SHOWN, re.sub(r"[^\w-]", "_", sid)) if sid else None
    shown = set(open(shown_f).read().split()) if shown_f and os.path.exists(shown_f) else set()
    tasks = build(skip_sid=sid)
    hits = search(prompt, tasks, hook.get("cwd"), sid, shown)
    got = {t["id"] for _, t in hits}  # keyword hits first, then meaning-only matches BM25 missed
    hits = (hits + [h for h in semantic(prompt, tasks, hook.get("cwd"), sid, shown) if h[1]["id"] not in got])[:TOP_K]
    if not hits:
        if args:
            print("no similar past work found")
        return
    print(render(hits))
    if shown_f:  # don't repeat the same memory every prompt in one session
        os.makedirs(SHOWN, exist_ok=True)
        with open(shown_f, "a") as fh:
            fh.write("".join(f"{t['id']}\n" for _, t in hits))


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: redaction, task split, ranking, threshold
    assert "[redacted]" in _redact("export [redacted] and "sk-" not in _redact("[redacted]")

"""footprint — learn a local SLM from your Claude Code transcripts.

Commands:
  setup                 create .venv + install the platform backend (mlx / torch)
  trace                 arm tracing: sessions from now on become training data (run before chatting)
  collect [project|--all]  curated training data: accepted turns + your own commits, redacted, split by session (default: this project)
  train                 LoRA v2 on data/ -> new adapter version (live only if test loss improves)
  eval                  test loss + perplexity of the footprint adapter on held-out data
  adapter [use vN]      list adapter versions (* = live) with losses; use vN = switch / roll back
  serve                 OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8399 (install runs this for you)
  install               auto-start server (launchd / systemd / Task Scheduler) + OpenCode /footprint
  context [install]     previous Claude session's state for this project; install = SessionStart hook
  bench [harvest|run|upload]  Claude-parity benchmark on your own tasks (any model)
  recall [text|--embed] similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt); --embed = index all for semantic search
  profile               what new sessions learn about you + this project (also part of `context`)
  recall [text]         similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt)
  memory list|forget|review|eval  what sessions are told about you (list [--all]); forget <id> drops a wrong
                        preference; review = mark each right/wrong; eval = correction rate, git outcomes, precision
  facts [--all]         structured memory: your stated preferences as JSON (hook: added at session start)
  switch [list|session] open latest (or chosen) Claude Code chat in OpenCode, full history; list = show ids
  status                what's collected/trained
  login [fp_key]        sign in with your website API key (no key = GitHub device flow)
  key list|revoke       list/revoke API keys (generate them on the website)
  sync push|pull [--with-data]  sync adapters/ (and, only if asked, training data/) via your vault
"""
import os, sys

from . import adapters, bench, config, context, memory, service, switch, transcripts, vault
from .backends import get


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if cmd == "train" and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl")):
        sys.exit("no data. run: footprint collect")
    {"collect": lambda: transcripts.collect(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else None),
     "trace": service.trace,
     "train": lambda: get().train(),
     "eval": lambda: get().evaluate(),
     "adapter": lambda: adapters.main(argv[1:]),
     "serve": lambda: get().serve(),
     "install": service.install,
     "context": lambda: context.show(argv[1:]),
     "switch": lambda: switch.switch(argv[1:]),
     "recall": lambda: memory.recall(argv[1:]),
     "profile": lambda: print(memory.profile(memory.build(), os.getcwd()) or "nothing learned yet"),
     "facts": lambda: memory.facts_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "memory": lambda: memory.memory_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "bench": lambda: bench.main(argv[1:]),
     "status": service.status,
     "setup": service.setup,
     "login": lambda: vault.login(argv[1:]),
     "key": lambda: vault.keys_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "sync": lambda: vault.sync_cmd(argv[1:])}.get(cmd, lambda: sys.exit(__doc__))()

                {"content": "add test", "status": "pending"}, {"content": "fix", "status": "completed"}]}}]}},
        {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "is_error": True, "content": "boom"}]}},
        {"type": "user", "isMeta": True, "message": {"role": "user", "content": "meta noise"}},
        {"type": "assistant", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "fixed, test next"}]}},
    ]
def profile(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Session-start block: who you are as a developer + what this project is. '' when nothing learned."""
    here = [t for t in tasks if cwd and t["cwd"] and os.path.abspath(t["cwd"]) == os.path.abspath(cwd)]
    out = []  # standing preferences come from facts() (evidence-based), not from here
    tools = Counter(h for t in tasks for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(8)
    exts = Counter(os.path.splitext(f)[1] for t in tasks for f in t["files"] if os.path.splitext(f)[1]).most_common(6)
    habits = []
    if tools:
        habits.append("tools you run: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in tools))
    if exts:
        habits.append("you mostly edit: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in exts))
    if habits:
        out.append("Habits: " + "; ".join(habits))
    from_repo = repo(cwd) if cwd and os.path.isdir(cwd) else []
    if here or from_repo:
        proj = [f"## This project: {os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(cwd))} ({len(here)} past tasks)", *from_repo]
        root = os.path.abspath(cwd) + os.sep
        hot = Counter(f[len(root):] if f.startswith(root) else f for t in here for f in t["files"]).most_common(8)
        if hot:
            proj.append("Most-edited files: " + ", ".join(f for f, _ in hot))
        tools = Counter(h for t in here for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(6)
        if tools:
            proj.append("Tools run here: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in tools))
        now = time.time()
        recent = sorted(here, key=lambda t: -t["t"])[:5]
        if recent:
            proj.append("Recent work here:\n" + "\n".join(
                f"- {(now - t['t']) / 86400:.0f}d ago: {' '.join(t['prompt'].split())[:140]}" for t in recent))
        out.append("\n".join(proj))
    if not out:
        return ""
    head = "# Your profile (footprint — learned from your past sessions; follow unless the user says otherwise)"
    return "\n\n".join([head, *out])[:config.PROFILE_CAP]


def facts(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Structured memory (schema v1): standing preferences the user stated in their own prompts.
    Derived from the task index on demand, so nothing is stored twice or goes stale.
    Same word-set across sessions = one record with more evidence; newest wording wins;
    seen in 2+ projects = user scope, else project scope. cwd filters to user + that project."""
    recs = {}
    for t in tasks:
        if kind(t["prompt"]) == "paste" or TEMP_PATH.match(t["cwd"] or "") or "/scratchpad" in (t["cwd"] or ""):
            continue  # a pasted doc's rules aren't the user's; nor are test prompts run in temp folders
        for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", t["prompt"]):
            s = s.strip(" -*>\t")
            if not (12 <= len(s) <= 200 and len(s.split()) >= 4 and PREF.search(s)) or s.startswith(("<", "{", '"')) \
                    or s.endswith("?") or '":' in s or re.search(r"never ?mind", s, re.I):
                continue
            key = " ".join(sorted(set(_words(s))))
            if not key:
                continue
            r = recs.setdefault(key, {"kind": "correction" if is_correction(t["prompt"]) else "preference",
                                      "text": s, "projects": set(), "evidence": [],
                                      "first": t["t"], "last": t["t"]})
            r["projects"].add(t["cwd"] or "?")
            r["evidence"].append(t["id"])
            r["first"] = min(r["first"], t["t"])
            if t["t"] >= r["last"]:
                r["text"], r["last"] = s, t["t"]
    here = os.path.abspath(cwd) if cwd else None
    gone = forgotten()
    day = lambda ts: datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).date().isoformat()
    now = max((t["t"] for t in tasks), default=0)  # decay against your latest activity, not the wall clock
    out = []
    for key, r in recs.items():
        n, projs = len(r["evidence"]), sorted(r["projects"])
        scope = "user" if len(projs) > 1 else f"project:{projs[0]}"
        fid = "f_" + hashlib.sha1(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
        if fid in gone:
            continue
        recency = 0.5 ** (max(0, now - r["last"]) / 86400 / HALF_LIFE)
        out.append({"id": fid, "score": round(SOURCE_W[r["kind"]] * min(1, n / 3) * recency, 3),
                    "polarity": "-" if NEG.search(r["text"]) else "+", "superseded_by": None,
                    "_fresh": recency >= STALE, "_cw": set(_words(r["text"])) - PREF_WORDS, "schema": 1, "kind": r["kind"],
                    "scope": scope, "text": r["text"], "count": n,
                    "confidence": round(min(0.95, 0.5 + 0.15 * (n - 1)), 2),  # ponytail: evidence-count prior
                    "evidence": r["evidence"][-5:], "first_seen": day(r["first"]), "last_seen": day(r["last"]),
                    "_last": r["last"]})
    # same subject, opposite polarity ("always use X" vs "never use X"): the newer one wins
    # ponytail: polarity only; "use pnpm" vs "use npm" (same polarity, rival tools) isn't caught
    # or same polarity, rival tools ("always use pnpm" then "always use bun"): the newer choice wins
    picks = lambda r, g: {w for w in g if re.search(rf"\b{w}\b", r["text"], re.I)}
    for a in out:
        for b in out:
            if a is b or a["scope"] != b["scope"] or b["_last"] <= a["_last"] or not a["_cw"]:
                continue
            flip = a["polarity"] != b["polarity"] and len(a["_cw"] & b["_cw"]) / len(a["_cw"] | b["_cw"]) >= 0.5
            rival = a["polarity"] == b["polarity"] == "+" and any(
                (pa := picks(a, g)) and (pb := picks(b, g)) and not pa & pb for g in RIVALS)
            if flip or rival:
                a["superseded_by"] = b["id"]
    for r in out:
        r["active"] = r["count"] >= FACT_MIN and not r["superseded_by"] and r.pop("_fresh")
        del r["_cw"]
    out = [r for r in out if not here or r["scope"] in ("user", f"project:{here}")]
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["active"], r["score"], r.pop("_last")), reverse=True)
    return out


def render_facts(recs, cap=1200):
    recs = [r for r in recs if r["active"]][:12]
    if not recs:
        return ""
    lines = ["# Standing preferences (footprint memory — stated by this user in past sessions; "
             "follow unless told otherwise)"]
    lines += [f"- {r['text']}" + (f" (x{r['count']})" if r["count"] > 1 else "") for r in recs]
    return "\n".join(lines)[:cap]


def facts_cmd(args=()):
    """`footprint facts [--all]` — structured memory as JSON (this project + user-wide; --all = every project)."""
    print(json.dumps(facts(build(), None if "--all" in args else os.getcwd()), indent=2))


def forgotten():
    try:
        return set(json.load(open(FORGOTTEN, encoding="utf-8")))


def memory_cmd(args=()):
    """`footprint memory list [--all]` — what new sessions are told about you; `forget <id>...` removes a wrong one."""
    sub, rest = (args[0] if args else "list"), list(args[1:])
    if sub == "forget":
        known = {f["id"] for f in facts(build())}
        ids = [i for i in rest if i in known]
        for i in set(rest) - known:
            print(f"unknown id {i} (see: footprint memory list --all)")
        if ids:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(FORGOTTEN), exist_ok=True)
            json.dump(sorted(forgotten() | set(ids)), open(FORGOTTEN, "w", encoding="utf-8"))
            print(f"forgot {len(ids)}: never injected again")
        return
    if sub == "eval":
        return print(evaluate(build(), os.getcwd()))
    if sub == "review":
        return review(build(), rest)
    if sub != "list":
        sys.exit("usage: footprint memory list [--all] | forget <id>... | review | eval")
    tasks, cwd = build(), os.getcwd()
    fs = facts(tasks, None if "--all" in rest else cwd)
    print("Standing preferences (injected at session start when seen x%d+):" % FACT_MIN)
    for f in fs:
        why = "on " if f["active"] else "replaced" if f["superseded_by"] else "once" if f["count"] < FACT_MIN else "stale"
        print(f"  [{why:<8}] {f['id']}  x{f['count']}  score {f['score']:.2f}  "
              f"{f['scope'].replace('project:', '')[-30:]:<30}  {f['text'][:90]}")
    if not fs:
        print("  (none yet)")
    print()
    print(profile(tasks, cwd) or "No profile yet.")
    if forgotten():
        print(f"\n{len(forgotten())} forgotten (edit {FORGOTTEN} to undo)")


def recall(args=()):
    """`footprint recall` — hook mode reads {prompt, cwd, session_id} JSON on stdin
    (Claude UserPromptSubmit / OpenCode plugin); by hand: footprint recall <text>."""
    hook = {}
    if args == ["--embed"]:
        tasks = build()
        n = len(embed_index(tasks, limit=len(tasks)))
        return print(f"{n}/{len({t['id'] for t in tasks})} tasks embedded with {config.EMBED_MODEL}" if n else
                     f"no embeddings — is Ollama running? try: ollama pull {config.EMBED_MODEL}")
    if args:
        hook = {"prompt": " ".join(args), "cwd": os.getcwd()}
    elif not sys.stdin.isatty():
        try:
            hook = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return
    prompt, sid = hook.get("prompt") or "", hook.get("session_id")
    if (os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MEMORY") == "off" or not prompt.strip() or context.HANDOFF_END in prompt
            or prompt.lstrip().startswith(context.NOISE)):  # harness messages (task notifications) aren't asks
        return
    shown_f = os.path.join(SHOWN, re.sub(r"[^\w-]", "_", sid)) if sid else None
    shown = set(open(shown_f).read().split()) if shown_f and os.path.exists(shown_f) else set()
    tasks = build(skip_sid=sid)
    hits = search(prompt, tasks, hook.get("cwd"), sid, shown)

    hits = (hits + [h for h in semantic(prompt, tasks, hook.get("cwd"), sid, shown) if h[1]["id"] not in got])[:TOP_K]
    if not hits:

            print("no similar past work found")

    if shown_f:  # don't repeat the same memory every prompt in one session

if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: redaction, task split, ranking, threshold

"""footprint — learn a local SLM from your Claude Code transcripts.

Commands:
  setup                 create .venv + install the platform backend (mlx / torch)
  trace                 arm tracing: sessions from now on become training data (run before chatting)
  collect [project|--all]  curated training data: accepted turns + your own commits, redacted, split by session (default: this project)
  train                 LoRA v2 on data/ -> new adapter version (live only if test loss improves)
  eval                  test loss + perplexity of the footprint adapter on held-out data
  adapter [use vN]      list adapter versions (* = live) with losses; use vN = switch / roll back
  serve                 OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8399 (install runs this for you)
  install               auto-start server (launchd / systemd / Task Scheduler) + OpenCode /footprint
  context [install]     previous Claude session's state for this project; install = SessionStart hook
  bench [harvest|run|upload]  Claude-parity benchmark on your own tasks (any model)
  recall [text|--embed] similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt); --embed = index all for semantic search
  profile               what new sessions learn about you + this project (also part of `context`)
  recall [text]         similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt)
  memory list|forget|review|eval  what sessions are told about you (list [--all]); forget <id> drops a wrong
                        preference; review = mark each right/wrong; eval = correction rate, git outcomes, precision
  facts [--all]         structured memory: your stated preferences as JSON (hook: added at session start)
  switch [list|session] open latest (or chosen) Claude Code chat in OpenCode, full history; list = show ids
  status                what's collected/trained
  login [fp_key]        sign in with your website API key (no key = GitHub device flow)
  key list|revoke       list/revoke API keys (generate them on the website)
  sync push|pull [--with-data]  sync adapters/ (and, only if asked, training data/) via your vault
"""
import os, sys

from . import adapters, bench, config, context, memory, service, switch, transcripts, vault
from .backends import get


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if cmd == "train" and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl")):
        sys.exit("no data. run: footprint collect")
    {"collect": lambda: transcripts.collect(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else None),
     "trace": service.trace,
     "train": lambda: get().train(),
     "eval": lambda: get().evaluate(),
     "adapter": lambda: adapters.main(argv[1:]),

     "facts": lambda: memory.facts_cmd(argv[1:]),

import json, math, os, re, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data")
ADAPTER_ROOT = os.path.join(ROOT, "adapters")
PROJECTS = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
TRACE_MARK = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/footprint-trace")
OPENCODE = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/opencode")
OPENCODE_DB = os.path.join(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share"),
                           "opencode", "opencode.db")
LAUNCHD = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.footprint.serve.plist")
SYSTEMD = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/systemd/user/footprint.service")

IS_MAC = sys.platform == "darwin"
IS_WIN = sys.platform == "win32"
VENV_PY = os.path.join(ROOT, ".venv", "Scripts", "python.exe") if IS_WIN \
    else os.path.join(ROOT, ".venv", "bin", "python")
ENTRY = os.path.join(ROOT, "footprint.py")

MODEL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MODEL",
                       "mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct-4bit" if IS_MAC
                       else "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct")
PORT = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_PORT", "8399")
# versioned adapters: adapters/<model>/vN/ + an `active` file naming the live one (switch = rollback)
MODEL_ADAPTERS = os.path.join(ADAPTER_ROOT, re.sub(r"[^\w.-]+", "--", MODEL))


def active_version():
    try:
        return open(os.path.join(MODEL_ADAPTERS, "active"), encoding="utf-8").read().strip() or None
    except OSError:
        return None


ADAPTERS = os.path.join(MODEL_ADAPTERS, active_version() or "none")  # what serve/eval use
LORA_RANK = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_LORA_RANK", "16"))
LORA_ALPHA = 2 * LORA_RANK
LEARNING_RATE = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_LR", "1e-4")
ITERS = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_ITERS")        # unset -> auto, epoch-based (resolve_iters)
EPOCHS = float(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_EPOCHS", "2"))  # 1-2 passes; best checkpoint by val loss = early stop
BATCH = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_BATCH", "1"))
ITERS_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_ITERS_CAP", "2000"))  # ceiling so big datasets stay tractable
TEST_BATCHES = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_TEST_BATCHES", "25"))  # eval subsample; -1 = whole test split
CTX_BUDGET = 6000      # chars of history per training example
RESULT_CAP = 1500      # chars kept per tool result
CONTEXT_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_CAP", "4000"))  # chars injected at session start (~1k tokens)
CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H = float(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H", "168"))  # older previous session = stale, skip
MEMORY_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MEMORY_CAP", "1500"))  # chars of similar past work injected per prompt
PROFILE_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_PROFILE_CAP", "1500"))  # chars of profile + project memory at session start
EMBED_MODEL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_EMBED_MODEL", "nomic-embed-text")  # Ollama; absent = BM25-only recall
OLLAMA_URL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434")

SYSTEM = ("You are footprint, a local coding agent. Use the provided tools to read, search, edit and run code "
          "in the user's project, then reply briefly with what you did.")
# OpenCode's own tool names + argument names: what the model is called with at runtime, so it trains on them
_t = lambda name, desc, props, req: {"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": name, "description": desc, "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": req}}}
_s = {"type": "string"}
TOOLS = [_t("bash", "Run a shell command", {"command": _s, "description": _s, "timeout": {"type": "number"}}, ["command"]),
         _t("read", "Read a file", {"filePath": _s, "offset": {"type": "number"}, "limit": {"type": "number"}}, ["filePath"]),
         _t("edit", "Replace text in a file", {"filePath": _s, "oldString": _s, "newString": _s,
                                               "replaceAll": {"type": "boolean"}}, ["filePath", "oldString", "newString"]),
         _t("write", "Write a whole file", {"filePath": _s, "content": _s}, ["filePath", "content"]),
         _t("grep", "Search file contents", {"pattern": _s, "path": _s, "include": _s}, ["pattern"]),
         _t("glob", "Find files by pattern", {"pattern": _s, "path": _s}, ["pattern"])]


def has_adapter():
    return active_version() is not None and any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(ADAPTERS, f))
               for f in ("adapters.safetensors", "adapter_model.safetensors"))


def ensure_test():
    """Path to the held-out test set (newest sessions, written by collect, never trained or validated on)."""
    test = os.path.join(DATA, "test.jsonl")
    if not os.path.exists(test):
        sys.exit("no test data. run: footprint collect")
    return test


def resolve_iters():
    """Training steps. FOOTPRINT_ITERS overrides; else EPOCHS passes over the
    train set (batch-1 => 1 step/example), clamped to [100, ITERS_CAP].
    Fixed 300 iters saw <1 epoch of a few-thousand-example set — this scales."""
    if ITERS:
        return str(ITERS)
    tr = os.path.join(DATA, "train.jsonl")
    n = sum(1 for _ in open(tr)) if os.path.exists(tr) else 0
    return str(max(100, min(ITERS_CAP, math.ceil(EPOCHS * n / max(BATCH, 1)))))


if __name__ == "__main__":  # sanity: ITERS override + clamp/epoch math
    globals()["ITERS"] = "42"; assert resolve_iters() == "42"
    _f = lambda n: max(100, min(2000, math.ceil(3.0 * n / 1)))
    assert _f(5713) == 2000   # big set hits cap
    assert _f(200) == 600     # mid set = 3 epochs
    assert _f(5) == 100       # tiny set floored
    print("resolve_iters clamp/epoch math ok")

content.text:
Lite plan is built. In lite mode, each project gets one `.md` file, and that file is the whole context layer. The self-check, the 5 tests and a live preview on this repo all pass. I haven't committed anything, and your own install is still on the full plan.

**How it works**
- `footprint context install --lite` turns it on. It saves the plan choice in `~/.footprint/plan`.
- Each project's file lives at `~/.footprint/context/<project>-<hash>.md`.
- **Every session start** (Claude Code hook or OpenCode plugin), footprint opens that file and keeps everything above the auto marker. That's the `## Notes` section, which you and the agent write.
- It then rewrites the part between the markers with your saved preferences, your profile, this project's memory and where the last session ended.
- It hands the whole file to the model, along with the file's path and one instruction: "when you learn something durable, append one line under `## Notes`." That's how the file keeps growing as you work.
- **The per-prompt "similar past work" step is off in lite mode.** The file replaces it.

**Changes**
- `footprint_core/context.py`: `md_path`, `write_md`, the lite branch in `show()`, and `install(lite)`.
- `footprint_core/config.py`: the `lite()` check, plus `FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MD` (where the files go) and `FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MD_CAP` (8000 characters).
- `footprint_core/memory.py`: `recall` does nothing in lite mode.
- The self-check now confirms your Notes survive a rewrite and the auto block gets replaced.

**Limits**
- The auto block only refreshes at session start. In the middle of a session, the file only changes when the agent adds Notes. A Stop hook that refreshes it at the end of each turn would fix that; I can add it if you want it to update live.
- If the file grows past 8000 characters, the model only sees the newest 8000. Nothing trims your Notes for you.

**Decision for you:** I put the files in `~/.footprint/context/` so prompt history doesn't end up in your repos. If you'd rather have `FOOTPRINT.md` in the project root, where git tracks it and teammates can share it, tell me and I'll switch it.

To try it on this machine: `python footprint.py context install --lite`

lastPrompt: FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MD_CAP (8000 characters). what is this "

content.text:
It's a size limit: how much of the `.md` file gets sent to the model when a session starts.

- **Why it exists:** whatever footprint hands the model fills up its context window. You and the agent keep adding Notes and the file never shrinks, so after a few months it could be 50k characters. Sending all of that every session would be slow and would leave less room for the actual work.
- **What it does:** if the file is longer than 8000 characters, only the **last** 8000 get sent. The file on disk stays complete, and nothing is deleted.
- **Why 8000:** that's about 2k tokens. It's twice the cap the full plan already uses at session start (4000), which seemed fair since the file now replaces the per-prompt step too.
- **How to change it:** `export FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MD_CAP=16000`.

**One catch:** the model sees the end of the file. The auto block is at the bottom and your Notes are at the top, so once the file passes 8000, the **oldest Notes get cut first**.

Better fix: cap only the auto block and always send the Notes in full. Want me to switch it to that?

**Overall: 7/10 as a product move, 3/10 for novelty.**

**What's good**
- **It's simple.** One file, no index to run, no Ollama, no per-prompt hook. Easy to install, debug and explain.
- **You can see and edit it.** The user reads exactly what the model is told and fixes it by hand. Enterprises and careful developers trust that more than a hidden index.
- **It works with any model,** whether that's Claude, OpenCode, a local model or GLM, at $0 cost to you.
- **It fits your own research.** `alternateApproach.md` already recommends "Approach C (learned profile) before LoRA", and this is that idea in its leanest form.
- **It cuts scope.** You've built a lot (LoRA v2, embeddings, bench, vault). Lite gives you something you can ship now.

**What's weak**
- **It isn't new.** `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, Cursor rules and Claude Code's own auto-memory (the one I'm using in this session) already do "an .md file the agent reads and writes". Nobody will pay for the file itself.
- **Agent-written notes decay.** The models will add obvious or one-off lines, duplicate each other, and rarely delete anything stale. In three months the Notes section is noise. Right now nothing cleans it up.
- **It depends on the agent obeying.** "Append to Notes" is only an instruction. Some models will ignore it, and others will write too much.
- **Without retrieval, it doesn't scale.** A file only holds so much, while the recall index searches every past task. Lite gives up "how did I solve this before?" in exchange for simplicity.

**Where your edge is:** not in the `.md` file, but in the **auto block**:
- the handover between Claude Code and OpenCode,
- preferences mined from your own prompts, and
- project habits learned from your history.

The file is just how that reaches the model. Pitch lite as "your sessions, distilled into one file any agent reads", not as "an md context layer".

**Before you commit to it:** run your bench three ways: no context, the lite `.md`, and the full plan with recall. If lite scores about the same as full, ship lite as the default and keep full as an extra. If full clearly wins, lite becomes the free tier.

**Fixes worth making:**
1. Always send the Notes in full and cap only the auto block. That's the issue from the cap question.
2. Run a cleanup pass every N sessions that merges duplicates and drops stale notes.

content.text:
No. Before today, footprint never kept context in a `.md` file.

**How footprint worked before today**
- Your past tasks were indexed in `~/.footprint/memory.json`, a JSON file.
- At each session start and on each prompt, footprint built the context text fresh from that index and printed it into the hook. Nothing was saved, so there was no file to read or edit.
- Its only `.md` files were OpenCode command definitions: `continue.md` for `/continue` and `footprint.md` for `/footprint`. Those define commands and hold no context.

**The `.md` files you've seen**
- **Claude Code's own memory.** Claude Code keeps notes about you and this project in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-aman-Developer-footprint/memory/` (`MEMORY.md` + `footprint-project.md`). That's a Claude Code feature, not part of footprint.
- **Other tools do this too.** `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and Cursor rules all work this way.

That's why I scored the idea low on novelty. The pattern already exists in those tools, but footprint itself hadn't used it.

Today's lite mode is the first time footprint writes a `.md` file of its own, and its version adds something those tools lack: the auto block is filled from your sessions in both Claude Code and OpenCode.

No. Lite mode doesn't touch Claude's files. It writes its own separate file.

| | Claude Code's memory | footprint lite (today) |
|---|---|---|
| File | `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/*.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | `~/.footprint/context/<project>-<hash>.md` |
| Who writes it | the Claude Code agent, based on its own judgment | footprint fills the auto block from your sessions; the agent adds Notes |
| Who reads it | Claude Code only | Claude Code (via the hook) and OpenCode (via the plugin) |
| Content | what Claude chose to remember | your saved preferences, profile, project memory, last-session handover, plus Notes |

It's the same pattern in a different file. footprint never reads or edits Claude's memory or `CLAUDE.md`.

**Another way to do it:** footprint could write its auto block into `AGENTS.md`, inside markers, instead of its own file. OpenCode, Codex and Cursor already read `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` can pull it in with an `@AGENTS.md` import.
- **Upside:** no hook or plugin needed, and it works in tools footprint doesn't support.
- **Downside:** it writes into the user's repo, where git sees it and the history ends up in commits.

I'd keep the separate file. Want the `AGENTS.md` version as an option?

content.text:
**The separate file (what's built now) is better.**

**Why the separate file wins**
- **Git noise.** The auto block changes every session: the handover, the "recent work" list. Inside `AGENTS.md`, every session would leave the repo with a diff, and someone would eventually commit it by accident.
- **Privacy.** The auto block holds your own prompts and your last session's goal. That belongs on your machine, not in a shared repo where teammates or the public can read it. Secrets get redacted, but plenty of personal text would still be in there.
- **It's yours.** Preferences like "you run pnpm" or "caveman style" describe you, not the project. Your teammates on the same repo would get your habits pushed onto them.
- **Your support covers it.** footprint already hooks into Claude Code and OpenCode, the two tools you target, so reaching other tools through `AGENTS.md` adds little.

**When `AGENTS.md` wins**
- For **team-wide, stable** knowledge: "tests run with pytest", "never touch `legacy/`". Those facts are about the repo, so they should live in it.

**Best of both, later:** keep the private auto block in footprint's file. Add a command like `footprint notes promote` that copies chosen Notes into `AGENTS.md`. Build that when a team actually asks for shared conventions; not needed now.

content.text:
Where the file lives doesn't change the score. The model sees the same text either way, and only the content moves the benchmark.

Checking `bench.py` turned up two bigger problems.

**1. Lite mode gives the bench almost nothing right now.**
- The bench runs each task in a fresh clone in a temp folder.
- The `.md` path is derived from the folder path, so every replay gets a new, empty file.
- The "this project" profile and the last-session handover are also looked up by folder, and they find nothing for the temp folder.
- `AGENTS.md` has the same problem: the clone is checked out at an old commit that doesn't contain it.

So in the bench, both options come out roughly equal to running with no context.

**2. The current "memory on" scores may be inflated.**
- When the bench replays an old task, recall can surface that same task, or later work built on it, from your history. Only the live session is excluded, not anything later than the task.
- The model can then be shown the answer before it starts. "Memory on" can win for the wrong reason.

**What I'd fix first:**
1. Give the bench a time cutoff, so memory only sees sessions from before the task.
2. Look up the profile, handover and `.md` by the original project's path, not the temp clone's.

After that, compare no context, lite and full. Those are honest numbers.

Want me to make both fixes? Bench and training are still running from last session, so the new runs would start after they finish.

content.text:
Lighter, yes. Better, not proven.

**What lite contains compared to full:**

| | Full | Lite |
|---|---|---|
| Session start: preferences, profile, project memory, handover | ✅ | ✅ same text |
| Notes (written by you and the agent) | ❌ | ✅ new |
| Per-prompt "similar past work" | ✅ | ❌ removed |

So **lite = full − per-prompt recall + Notes.**

**Why it's lighter:**
- One read per session instead of a search on every prompt.
- No embeddings and no Ollama.
- Fewer tokens per prompt.

**Why "better" is unproven:**
- **Recall is the part that's tied to your current task:** "last time you fixed the date picker in `dob-picker.tsx` with `fromYear`". The `.md` file is general and can't do that.
- **Notes are the only thing lite adds,** and they're only as good as what the agent writes. With no cleanup they'll fill with noise over time.
- **There's no benchmark yet.** The bench can't test lite until the two fixes from my last answer are in (look up the `.md` by the real project path, and cut off memory at the task's date).

**My bet:** lite will score close to full on "work the way I work" tasks and lose on "I've solved this before" tasks. If the gap is small, lite should be the default because it's simpler and cheaper.

Make the two bench fixes and I'll get you the real numbers.

content.text:
Right, and it's not just lite. Neither context mode uses the GPU in any meaningful way.

**Where the GPU goes:**

| What runs | GPU use |
|---|---|
| Lite context (read the `.md`, rebuild the auto block) | **none.** Plain Python file reads, CPU only, milliseconds. |
| Full context (keyword search + optional Ollama embeddings) | **tiny.** One small embedding call per prompt, and only if Ollama is running. |
| **The model answering** | **this is the main load,** if it's local (Qwen + LoRA via MLX). A cloud model (Claude, OpenCode's cloud models) uses none of your GPU. |
| **LoRA training** (running now) | **heavy.** It takes nearly all of the GPU. |

**For a smoke test or bench run:**
- GPU load depends on **which model** you test, not on lite or full.
- A cloud model barely touches your GPU in either mode.
- The local footprint model is heavy in either mode.
- Lite's only saving is the small per-prompt embedding call. That shows up in CPU time, not the GPU.
- The bench and training are currently sharing the machine. That's why training was down to about 0.04 steps per second last session.

So lite isn't the fix for GPU load. It cuts complexity and tokens. If the GPU is what you're worried about, run the bench after training finishes, or test a cloud model.

{"additions":422,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBaW8Qg","is_bot":false,"login":"MRG15","name":""},"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Why

Two problems showed up while using footprint:

1. **Training looked endless.** `footprint train` printed raw log lines with no percent or time left. A real run took ~25 min at ~11 s/step and was stopped 2 minutes before the end — all work lost, no adapter.
2. **Memory was one big JSON file**, fully re-read and re-written on every prompt. Fine at 500 tasks, slow and crash-prone at 50k.

## What changed

### Memory → SQLite (`footprint_core/memory.py`)
| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `~/.footprint/memory.json` + `embed.json` | one file: `~/.footprint/memory.db` |
| whole file rewritten every prompt | only changed sessions rewritten |
| a crash mid-save could corrupt it | SQLite transactions + WAL (hook and OpenCode plugin can share it) |

- Embeddings live in the same file as float32 blobs. Old JSON caches are migrated once (vectors kept), then removed.
- `build()` still returns the same task list, so `search`, `facts`, `profile`, `recall` are untouched.
- **Not using sqlite-vec on purpose:** macOS system Python can't load SQLite extensions. Cosine runs in Python; fine at current sizes. Revisit past ~50k tasks.

### Training (`backends/mlx_backend.py`, mirrored in `torch_backend.py`)
| Setting | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Progress | raw mlx lines | `step 40/126 · 32% · ~15 min left` | user knows what's happening |
| Stop / crash | everything lost | resumes from last checkpoint on next `footprint train` | `progress.json` + `step<N>.safetensors`; Ctrl-C and SIGTERM handled |
| LoRA layers | all 28 | last half (`FOOTPRINT_LORA_LAYERS`) | late layers carry style; ~2× faster |
| Max seq length | fixed 4096 | fitted to the user's longest lesson (×256, 512–4096) | differs per person; nothing truncated, no wasted compute |
| Grad checkpoint | always on | `auto`: memory estimate vs RAM; OOM → retry with it on + resume | on a 16 GB M2 it's needed (OOM without it); on 32 GB it's skipped for speed |
| Early stop | always, even on 1 validation example | only with ≥10 validation examples (`FOOTPRINT_MIN_EVAL`) | 1 example = noise |

Every finished version's `metrics.json` now records `layers`, `seq`, `grad_ckpt`, `early_stop`.

### Collect (`transcripts.py`)
- New `split()`: validation and test grow by whole sessions until each has max(10, 10%) examples, while train keeps ≥60%. Before, 4 sessions gave **1** validation example.

### Docs / CI
- README: new env vars, `memory.db`, resume note, `FOOTPRINT_EPOCHS` default corrected to `2`.
- CI compiles every module (was a hand-picked subset), with `shell: bash` so the glob works on Windows.

## How it was tested
- Self-checks pass: `config`, `adapters` (new resume cases), `memory` (new SQLite store + migration cases), `context`.
- `pytest`: 8 pass (3 new for `split()`).
- **Real run on a 16 GB M2, 79 examples, 50 steps:**
  - grad checkpoint off → out of memory at step 1 → auto-retried with it on ✔
  - ~6 s/step (was ~11) with half the layers ✔
  - stopped at step 30 with SIGTERM → `stopped at step 25/50` → re-ran → `resuming v1 from step 25/50` → finished, test loss 2.283 ✔
- Real `footprint recall` against the new `memory.db`: 42 tasks indexed, hits returned in ~0.3 s ✔
- ⚠️ **Not run:** the torch (Linux/Windows) training path — same changes, but no torch env here. Worth one run on a Linux box before release.

## Rollout notes
- No action needed from users: first run of the new code builds `memory.db` from the transcripts and removes the old JSON files.
- An **unfinished** adapter folder from an older run (no `metrics.json`) is wiped and reused on the next `train`, because its LoRA shape (all layers) can't be resumed with the new default (half).
- Installed copies (`~/.footprint/app`) pick this up on the next install/update.

## Where to look first
1. `memory.p

content.text:
PR #8 is safe to merge, with a few caveats below. It's lined up correctly with `main`: it's one commit (`0d6288d`, by MRG15) on top of the latest `main` (`001e99f`). GitHub shows it as mergeable with no conflicts, and CI passes on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. I also ran it in a separate copy of the repo: the config, adapters, context and memory self-checks pass, and pytest passes 8 of 8. Nothing else in the codebase still points at the old `memory.json`.

**It doesn't affect lite mode.** `context.py` isn't touched, and the lite check in `recall` is still there.

**What changes (9 files, +422 / −94)**

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| **Memory** | `memory.json` + `embed.json` are replaced by one `~/.footprint/memory.db` (SQLite). Only changed sessions are rewritten, and embeddings are stored in the same file. The old JSON files are migrated once and then deleted. |
| **Training (MLX)** | Shows progress as `step 40/126 · 32% · ~15 min left`. A run stopped by Ctrl-C or a crash resumes from its last checkpoint. LoRA goes on the last half of the layers by default, which is about 2× faster. Max length is fitted to your longest training example instead of a fixed 4096. Grad checkpointing turns on automatically when memory is tight, and an out-of-memory crash retries with it on. |
| **Early stop** | Only used when there are at least 10 validation examples. |
| **Collect** | The new `split()` grows the validation and test sets to max(10, 10%) of examples, while train keeps at least 60%. |
| **Torch backend** | Same changes for Linux and Windows. |
| **CI / README** | CI now compiles every module. README documents the new settings. |

**Caveats**
1. **The torch path was never run.** The PR author says so too. Linux and Windows training could break, so it needs one real run on Linux before release.
2. **Half the layers is a quality bet.** "Late layers carry style" is the author's claim, not something they measured. The test-loss gate keeps a worse adapter from going live, but v3 might simply never beat v1.
3. **Yesterday's unfinished v2 gets deleted** on the next `train`, with the message "discarding unfinished v2". It was never usable, so nothing of value is lost.
4. **Reads aren't any faster.** Each prompt still loads every task from the database; only the writes are incremental. The "slow at 50k" problem is half fixed.
5. **Small one:** after a resume, the optimizer state starts fresh. The loss may jump for a few steps, with no lasting harm.

Want me to merge it and then restart training on the new code?

content.text:
Haan, Windows pe pehle bhi PyTorch hi tha. Mac pe MLX chalta hai, aur baaki sab (Linux, Windows) pe `torch_backend.py`. Ye `backends/__init__.py` mein decide hota hai: `IS_MAC` → MLX, warna → torch.

**PR se pehle Windows/Linux pe kya tha (`main` pe abhi bhi yahi hai):**

| Part | Kaise |
|---|---|
| Setup | `footprint setup` ~2 GB install karta hai: `torch transformers peft trl datasets` |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct`, full precision. Mac wala 4-bit version nahi. |
| Train | HF `SFTTrainer` + LoRA rank 16, saari layers (`all-linear`), max length 4096, grad checkpointing hamesha on, best checkpoint by val loss |
| GPU | CUDA mila to GPU (`device_map="auto"`), nahi to **CPU**. CPU pe training bahut slow hogi, ghanton se dinon tak. |
| Serve | OpenAI-style API, PyTorch `generate()` se |
| Auto-start | Windows pe Task Scheduler, Linux pe systemd |

**Ye path kabhi test nahi hua:**
- CI Windows pe sirf modules compile karta hai aur `status` + `trace` chalata hai. Real training kabhi nahi chali.
- Matlab Windows training `main` pe bhi kabhi verify nahi hui. PR ne ek naya risk nahi dala; pehle wala untested code aur bada kar diya.

**PR ke baad Windows pe kya badlega:**
- Saari layers ki jagah aakhri aadhi layers, aur max length data se fit hogi.
- RAM detection Windows pe fail hota hai, kyunki `os.sysconf` wahan exist hi nahi karta. Error pakda jaata hai, to grad checkpointing on rehta hai. Safe hai, bas thoda slow.
- Out of memory hone pe grad checkpointing on karke retry karta hai.
- Resume: HF ke apne `checkpoint-*` folders se, plus `progress.json`.
- Ctrl-C ka handling sirf MLX mein hai. Torch pe stop karoge to progress na bachne ka risk hai, aur ye untested hai.

**Suggestion:** merge karne se pehle ek Linux machine pe chhota run kar lo (50 steps). Ek GitHub Actions job bhi chal sakta hai jo CPU pe 5 steps train kare, ~10 min. Bolo to woh CI job add kar doon?
